notes: EBIT is approximated as “Operating income” (GAAP) from Target’s consolidated statements/MD&A tables. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/27419/000002741926000016/tgt-20260131.htm))

D&A equals “Depreciation and amortization” from Target’s consolidated cash flow statement; capex equals “Expenditures for property and equipment.” ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/27419/000002741926000016/tgt-20260131.htm))

NWC is computed as (Inventory + Other current assets) - (Accounts payable + Accrued and other current liabilities) using year-end balance sheet line items; sign is negative due to retailer working-capital structure. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/27419/000002741926000016/tgt-20260131.htm))

Investments is left null because the balance sheet presentation used here does not provide a clearly isolatable standalone “investments” line item suitable for adding to equity in a standard DCF bridge. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/27419/000002741926000016/tgt-20260131.htm))

NOL balance uses disclosed gross tax loss carryforwards (Canada + Luxembourg) and assigns a conservative low utilization rate due to the disclosure noting remote possibility of realization. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/27419/000002741926000016/tgt-20260131.htm))

WACC, terminal growth, and terminal value methodology are modeled assumptions (not explicitly provided by the company) and are set to conventional, conservative retail levels for a base-case. ([corporate.target.com](https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/03/target-corporation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-earnings))
Current price set to $113.26 (latest available from the market data pull used in this run).

catalysts: Sustained comparable sales improvement and inventory normalization driving less promotional markdown pressure.
Operating leverage from disciplined cost management while maintaining investment in stores, supply chain, and digital capabilities.
company_overview: Target serves guests at nearly 2,000 stores and at Target.com. ([corporate.target.com](https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/03/target-corporation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-earnings))

Revenue model includes merchandise sales plus non-merchandise revenues such as advertising and credit card profit-sharing income. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/27419/000002741926000016/tgt-20260131.htm))
Company fiscal year ends in late January/early February (52/53-week year convention). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/27419/000002741926000016/tgt-20260131.htm))
current_context: FY2025: Net sales declined 1.7% to $104.8B and full-year operating income fell 8.1% to $5.1B. ([corporate.target.com](https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/03/target-corporation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-earnings))

FY2025 effective income tax rate was 22.3% (vs. 22.2% in 2024). ([corporate.target.com](https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/03/target-corporation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-earnings))

FY2026 guidance: net sales growth around 2%, and full-year operating income margin rate ~20 bps higher than the 4.6% adjusted operating income margin rate in 2025. ([corporate.target.com](https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/03/target-corporation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-earnings))
FY2026 capital expenditures expected to be approximately $5B. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/27419/000002741926000016/tgt-20260131.htm))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth is anchored to management’s FY2026 “around 2%” net sales growth guidance and then moderates slightly. ([corporate.target.com](https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/03/target-corporation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-earnings))

EBIT margin stabilizes around the guided 2026 level (~4.8% implied by guidance vs. 4.6% adjusted in 2025) with modest improvement thereafter. ([corporate.target.com](https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/03/target-corporation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-earnings))

D&A and capex scale with sales; capex intensity is aligned to the $5B FY2026 investment expectation and then tapers. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/27419/000002741926000016/tgt-20260131.htm))

Working capital is modeled as consistently negative as a percent of sales, reflecting Target’s inventory and supplier financing dynamics (observed in the historical balance sheet build). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/27419/000002741926000016/tgt-20260131.htm))
key_risks: Merchandising pressures (markdown intensity, purchase order/availability risk) that compress gross margin and operating income.
Consumer demand softness and competitive pricing that slows net sales growth below base-case expectations.
Execution risk in store/supply-chain investments and the resulting impact on capex productivity and margins.

valuation_summary: DCF terminal assumptions use a conservative gordon_growth framework (low terminal growth) consistent with a mature retail platform. ([corporate.target.com](https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/03/target-corporation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-earnings))

Scenario analysis stresses sensitivity through WACC and terminal growth, plus modest near-term operating/margin deviations around management’s guidance range. ([corporate.target.com](https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/03/target-corporation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-earnings))
